bib.title: Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them: Overcoming Few-Shot Prompt Order Sensitivity
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 8086-8098

question: How much does the order of few-shot examples in an in-context prompt change classification accuracy, and can good orders be chosen without a labelled development set?
hypothesis: Prompt order sensitivity is a fundamental property of in-context learning, and an unlabelled probing set generated by the model itself can rank orderings well enough to pick performant ones.
contributions: We study order sensitivity for In-context Learning, which we show is crucial for the success of pretrained language models for few-shot learning.
We propose a simple, generation-based probing method to identify performant prompts without requiring additional data.

Our probing method is universally applicable and effective across different sizes of pretrained language models and for different types of datasets - achieving on average a 13% relative improvement over a wide range of tasks.

method.summary: For a random set of 4 training examples, all 24 orderings are used as prompts; each prompt is sampled from the LM (temperature 2) to build an unlabelled probing set. Orderings are ranked by GlobalE (entropy of predicted label distribution over the probing set) or LocalE (mean per-item prediction entropy), and the top 4 of 24 are used for evaluation on 11 classification datasets.
method.task: few-shot text classification via in-context learning; prompt order selection

datasets.name: SST-2, SST-5, MR, CR, MPQA, Subj, TREC, AGNews, DBPedia, CB, RTE
datasets.split: validation set subset; training examples (k-shot) drawn at random, 5 sets
datasets.source: Socher 2013; Pang and Lee 2004/2005; Hu and Liu 2004; Wiebe 2005; Voorhees and Tice 2000; Zhang 2015; De Marneffe 2019; Dagan 2005

models.name: GPT-3
models.params: 2.7B, 175B in main experiments (Figs 1 and 4 also show 6.7B and 13B)

inference.decoding: probing set: sampling with temperature 2 and block n-gram repetition; stop at template end-of-sentence token or length limit; classification: argmax over label set
inference.samples: 24 permutations x 5 random training sets = 120 runs per experiment; GPT-3 175B: 2 sets x 12 permutations; mean and std over sets
inference.prompting: 4-shot for all datasets except 1-shot DBPedia and 2-shot AGNews (Table 2 caption); template T(x,y)=input:x type:y for probing

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy on 256-example validation subset, mean and std over 5 sets

metrics.name: relative improvement
metrics.definition: improvement of selected prompts over mean of all candidate prompts, averaged over eleven tasks

eval.protocol: Mean and standard deviation over 5 random training sets; no significance test stated

prompts.text: Review: {Sentence} Sentiment: {Label} (templates 1 and 3, label words positive/negative or good/bad); Input: {Sentence} Prediction: {Label} (template 2); {Sentence} It was {Label} (template 4)

results.quote: some permutations have comparable performance (over 85% accuracy) to supervised training for sentiment classification, while others perform close to random (around 50%).

results.claim: GlobalE gives an average relative improvement across eleven tasks.
results.setup: Table 2, all GPT-2 and GPT-3 sizes, 4 of 24 selected orders vs mean of all 24
results.quote: GlobalE achieves, on average, a 13% relative improvement across the eleven dif-

results.claim: LocalE gives a slightly smaller average relative improvement than GlobalE.
results.quote: LocalE provides results slightly inferior to GlobalE, with an average 9.6% relative improvement over the baseline model.

results.claim: A specific permutation drops sharply when the model changes from GPT2-XL to GPT2-Large.
results.setup: SST-2, 4-shot, one permutation, GPT2-XL (1.5B) vs GPT2-Large (0.8B)
results.quote: a specific permuta- tion's performance may drop from 88.7% to 51.6%
results.note: quote is the model's score for GPT2-XL; 51.6 is for GPT2-Large

results.claim: Order rank correlation between 175B and 2.7B is near zero.
results.setup: SST-2, 24 permutations, pairwise Spearman across 8 model sizes (Fig 4)
results.quote: the 175B and 2.7B model only has a correlation of 0.05

results.claim: GPT2-XL surpasses 90% accuracy on SST-2 with four examples for the best order.
results.quote: We see that the GPT2-XL (1.5B) model can even surpass 90% accuracy given just four samples.

results.claim: Supervised finetuning seeds typically vary by under 1% std, versus large order variance.
results.quote: less than 1% standard deviation for their test set

results.claim: Calibration raises accuracy but variance remains high; majority of failing prompts predict an unbalanced label distribution.
results.setup: SST-2, GPT2-XL, 2-shot calibrated (Zhao et al. 2021) over all permutations
results.quote: the majority of failing prompts suffer from highly unbalanced predicted label distributions (Figure 6, left).

results.claim: Adding training samples raises accuracy but variance remains and can grow.
results.setup: SST-2, GPT-2 family, 1-32 shots, at most 24 orderings sampled (Fig 3)
results.quote: a high level of variance remains, even with a large number of samples and can even increase.

results.claim: Performant label orderings are not consistent across models.
results.setup: SST-2, six label patterns, Spearman across model sizes (Fig 5)
results.quote: It is thus not possible to identify a label

limits: The paper has no limitations section.

Probing requires sampling from the model for each of the n! orderings (24 for four examples), so cost grows factorially with shots; only 4-shot (1-2 shot for DBPedia/AGNews) tested because of the 1024 word-piece GPT-2 context.
Only classification tasks; GPT-3 175B uses 2 sets x 12 permutations because of cost; no significance tests.
On CB and RTE the GPT-2 models are near random and gains are within random guess or majority vote levels.
Order sensitivity study (Figs 1-5) uses one fixed 4-example SST-2 set for visualisation; other sets only summarised as variance in Section 5.
Models are GPT-2 and GPT-3 (2021); instruction-tuned models were not studied.
